title: Cloudflare Makes Internal DNS Generally Available
gist: Cloudflare has taken Internal DNS to GA after a beta running since June 2025, pairing a Gateway Resolver for policy with an Internal Authoritative DNS for private zones and pitching consolidation of public and private DNS onto one control plane with a unified API and audit trail. It is free but restricted to enterprise customers - a gating decision that drew community accusations of breaking Cloudflare's no-enterprise-only-features promise - and targets accounts currently using Route 53, Azure Private DNS or Google Cloud DNS.

insights.claim: Cloudflare has taken its Internal DNS service - cloud-native authoritative and recursive DNS for private networks - to general availability after a private and public beta that began in June 2025, roughly a thirteen-month beta.
insights.speaker: Gianmarco Nalin
insights.so_what: Marks Cloudflare's formal entry into private enterprise networking, a segment previously ceded to AWS, Azure and Google Cloud.
insights.locator: Cloudflare has announced the general availability

insights.claim: The service splits into two components with deliberately separate jobs: a Gateway Resolver that enforces DNS security and routing policy, and Internal Authoritative DNS that manages zones.
insights.speaker: Gianmarco Nalin
insights.so_what: The policy/authority split is the architectural pattern to compare against Route 53 Resolver plus private hosted zones.
insights.quote: Cloudflare Internal DNS consists of two components: Gateway Resolver and Internal Authoritative DNS.

insights.claim: Both components are built on the same platform Cloudflare has operated for the last decade, letting the company monetise a decade of public-DNS scale experience in a new private-network product.
insights.speaker: Gianmarco Nalin
insights.so_what: Marginal-cost expansion off existing infrastructure is why Cloudflare can bundle this at no extra charge and pressure incumbents.
insights.locator: The authors explain that the two components

insights.claim: Users work with three entities - internal zones holding authoritative records for private resources, DNS views composing zones for specific use cases, and resolver policies stored in the gateway resolver that match and forward requests.
insights.speaker: Gianmarco Nalin
insights.so_what: DNS views make split-horizon setups work without running parallel systems, removing a common source of configuration drift.
insights.locator: Users can operate on three different entities

insights.claim: Resolution follows a defined path: the gateway resolver evaluates policies first and can block or forward, matched requests go to the internal authoritative DNS, unmatched ones route to the public path, and views can optionally fall back to public resolution.
insights.speaker: Gianmarco Nalin
insights.so_what: Public fallback lowers migration risk - teams can adopt internal zones incrementally without breaking name resolution.
insights.locator: A new DNS request is initially evaluated

themes.theme: Single control plane as the pitch

insights.claim: Cloudflare's core claim is consolidation of private and public DNS onto a single control plane with a unified API, audit trail, and policy registry.
insights.speaker: Gianmarco Nalin
insights.so_what: Consolidation is the wedge against best-of-breed DNS tooling; audit-trail unification is the compliance-team selling point.
insights.locator: It promises to consolidate both private and public DNSs

insights.claim: Configuration changes follow the same unified ingress whether they originate from the dashboard, a Terraform module, or a direct API call, which Cloudflare positions as simplifying audits.
insights.speaker: Gianmarco Nalin
insights.so_what: Single-ingress guarantees are what make DNS change auditability defensible to regulators and incident reviewers.
insights.locator: The company states that changes to the DNS configuration

insights.claim: Internal DNS is available only to enterprise-level customers, though at no additional charge, and is managed via console, Terraform or the Cloudflare API.
insights.speaker: Gianmarco Nalin
insights.so_what: Free-but-enterprise-gated is a land-grab pricing move aimed at displacing hyperscaler DNS inside accounts Cloudflare already holds.
insights.locator: Cloudflare Internal DNS is available to all enterprise-level customers

insights.claim: Community reaction on Reddit accused Cloudflare of abandoning its stated commitment not to launch enterprise-only features, a reputational cost of the gating decision.
insights.speaker: Gianmarco Nalin
insights.so_what: Developer-goodwill erosion is a real if unpriced risk for a company whose bottom-up adoption funnel depends on self-serve users.
insights.quote: Whatever happened to "No more enterprise only features"... Seems that plan has been tossed out the window.

insights.claim: Other commenters argued the product is niche with use cases unclear outside organisations running large internal networks, questioning the addressable market beyond big enterprises.
insights.speaker: Gianmarco Nalin
insights.so_what: If the TAM really is confined to large internal networks, this is a retention and account-expansion play rather than a new revenue line.
insights.quote: this is a pretty niche product, and the use cases aren't immediately clear unless you're dealing with a large internal network
insights.locator: In the same thread, ninadpathak highlights

insights.claim: The incumbent alternatives are provider-specific: Route 53 Resolver and private hosted zones on AWS, Private DNS and DNS Private Resolver on Azure, and private, forwarding and peering zones in Google Cloud DNS.
insights.speaker: Gianmarco Nalin
insights.so_what: Cloudflare's differentiation is cloud-neutrality - the pitch lands hardest with multicloud estates paying three DNS control planes today.
insights.locator: Developers and IT teams running their workloads on other cloud providers
